title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips MLROs, compliance and financial crime teams to run an effective, risk-based financial crime framework that uses AI responsibly, counters AI-enabled crime and evidences effectiveness to supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip financial crime professionals with a practical command of the risk-based approach and of how AI is changing both the threat and the tools used to counter it. Participants leave able to strengthen risk assessment, due diligence, monitoring, screening and reporting, govern AI-driven controls, and show supervisors that the firm's framework works in practice, not just on paper.
sections.What It Covers: The risk-based approach and FATF standards, business-wide risk assessment, customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring and machine learning, sanctions and adverse media screening, fraud and authorised push payment scams, deepfakes and synthetic identity, generative-AI-enabled crime, model governance for AML tools, suspicious activity reporting, and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.
Intended Audience: MLROs, deputy MLROs and heads of financial crime compliance
Financial crime, AML, sanctions and fraud analysts, investigators and team leaders
Compliance, risk, data and technology staff who design, validate or run financial crime systems
Learning Objectives: Apply the risk-based approach and FATF standards to the firm's business-wide risk assessment and controls
Design proportionate customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence, including digital identity verification
Evaluate machine learning in transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and fraud detection
Identify AI-enabled threats, including deepfakes, synthetic identities and generative-AI-enabled scams
Govern AI-driven financial crime tools through model risk management, explainability and fairness testing
Evidence the effectiveness of the financial crime framework to the board and supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine briefings with typology case studies, alert and report review exercises and group workshops, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and risk profile.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of AML, sanctions or fraud compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

modules.title: The Risk-Based Approach and Supervisory Expectations
modules.summary: The foundations of an effective financial crime framework: FATF standards, the risk-based approach, the MLRO's role and how supervisors now judge effectiveness rather than technical compliance alone.
objectives: Explain FATF standards and the risk-based approach as they apply to the firm
Define the accountabilities of the board, senior management and MLRO
Distinguish technical compliance from effectiveness in supervisory assessment
syllabus: FATF Recommendations, immediate outcomes and national risk assessments
Governance, MLRO independence, resourcing and accountability
How supervisors assess financial crime frameworks
Seeing the firm's controls the way a supervisor does

modules.title: Business-Wide Risk Assessment
modules.summary: Building a business-wide risk assessment that genuinely drives controls and resourcing, drawing on data rather than assertion and covering money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions, proliferation financing and fraud.
objectives: Design a business-wide risk assessment methodology linked to controls
Use customer, product, channel and geographic data to evidence inherent risk
Assess control effectiveness and residual risk credibly
syllabus: Inherent risk factors: customers, products, channels and geographies
Data-driven risk scoring and its limitations
Control effectiveness testing and residual risk
Linking the assessment to risk appetite, policy and resourcing

modules.title: Customer Due Diligence and Digital Identity
modules.summary: Proportionate customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence in a digital onboarding world, including beneficial ownership, politically exposed persons and the reliability of remote identity verification.
objectives: Apply risk-based CDD, EDD and ongoing monitoring
Evaluate digital identity verification and its vulnerabilities
Identify beneficial ownership and politically exposed person risks
syllabus: CDD, simplified and enhanced due diligence and periodic review
Beneficial ownership, complex structures and PEP screening
Remote onboarding, biometrics and FATF digital identity guidance
Perpetual KYC and event-driven review

modules.title: Transaction Monitoring and Machine Learning
modules.summary: How rules-based and machine learning approaches to transaction monitoring work, what they can realistically achieve, and how to tune, test and combine them to improve detection rather than just reduce alerts.
objectives: Compare rules-based, machine learning and network analytics approaches
Evaluate tuning, thresholds and false positive reduction claims
Design alert handling and investigation workflows that support quality
syllabus: Scenario design, thresholds and below-the-line testing
Supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection and graph analytics
False positives versus missed detection: measuring true performance
Alert triage, case management and AI-assisted investigation

modules.title: Sanctions Screening and Adverse Media
modules.summary: Designing and calibrating sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, including fuzzy matching and natural language processing, and managing evasion risks from ownership structures and trade.
objectives: Calibrate name and payment screening, including fuzzy matching
Evaluate natural language processing for adverse media monitoring
Identify sanctions evasion typologies relevant to the firm
syllabus: Screening lists, matching logic and threshold calibration
Ownership and control, and circumvention through intermediaries
Adverse media analytics and alert quality
Testing and assuring screening effectiveness

modules.title: Fraud and Authorised Push Payment Scams
modules.summary: The fraud threats facing firms and their customers, especially authorised push payment scams and money mules, and how behavioural analytics and real-time scoring help to stop losses.
objectives: Identify fraud typologies, including authorised push payment scams and mule networks
Evaluate real-time fraud scoring and behavioural analytics
Align fraud and AML functions to share intelligence and protect customers
syllabus: Investment, romance, impersonation and purchase scams
Money mule detection and account takeover
Behavioural biometrics, device intelligence and payee verification
Customer protection, reimbursement and fraud and AML convergence

modules.title: Deepfakes, Synthetic Identities and AI-Enabled Crime
modules.summary: How criminals use generative AI to create synthetic identities, forge documents, impersonate customers and executives, and scale social engineering, and how the firm builds resilience.
objectives: Recognise generative-AI-enabled typologies and red flags
Assess the resilience of onboarding and authentication to deepfakes
Design layered controls and staff awareness against AI-enabled attacks
syllabus: Synthetic identities and AI-generated documents
Voice and video deepfakes in onboarding and executive impersonation
AI-generated phishing, scam content and automated social engineering
Liveness detection, call-back controls and layered defences

modules.title: Governing AI in Financial Crime Compliance
modules.summary: Applying model risk management to AI-driven financial crime tools, so that the firm can explain, validate, monitor and defend them, and avoid unfair or discriminatory outcomes.
objectives: Apply model risk management to AML, screening and fraud models
Evaluate explainability, human oversight and audit trails
Assess bias and de-risking effects on customers
syllabus: Model inventory, validation and performance monitoring
Explainability for investigators, auditors and supervisors
Vendor tools, data quality and third-party dependency
Bias, financial exclusion and unwarranted de-risking

modules.title: Suspicious Activity Reporting and Intelligence Sharing
modules.summary: Producing high-quality suspicious activity reports, working effectively with the national FIU and law enforcement, and using public-private partnerships and information sharing to improve detection.
objectives: Apply reporting thresholds and write high-quality, useful reports
Manage tipping-off, consent and exit decisions
Use information sharing and partnerships to improve intelligence
syllabus: Suspicion, reporting thresholds and report quality
Working with the national FIU and law enforcement
Tipping-off, defensive reporting and relationship exit
Public-private partnerships and privacy-preserving data sharing

modules.title: Evidencing Effectiveness to Supervisors
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by showing how to measure, test and report the effectiveness of the financial crime framework, prepare for supervisory review and plan the next stage of AI adoption.
objectives: Define metrics and management information that demonstrate effectiveness
Prepare for supervisory inspections, thematic reviews and independent reviews
Produce a financial crime and AI action plan for the firm
syllabus: Effectiveness metrics, quality assurance and board reporting
Common supervisory findings and remediation programmes
Inspection readiness: files, walkthroughs and interviews
Workshop: the firm's financial crime and AI action plan

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.

related.title: Sanctions Compliance
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.
